neighbours.label: come, came or drawing when an activity is about to end ('came to a halt', 'drawing to a close')
fire: By late autumn the harvest season was drawing to a close.
Negotiations between the two unions came to an abrupt end on Tuesday.
The entire project came to a standstill when funding ran out.
Traffic on the bridge came to a complete halt during the storm.
Her long career in the theatre is coming to an end this year.
All production at the plant comes to a stop during the holiday.
That era of cheap energy has come to a close at last.
The school term is drawing to an end for most students.
quiet: By late autumn the harvest workers were walking to the village.
Delegates from the two unions came to the capital on Tuesday.
The entire family came to the wedding when the invitations went out.
Tourists from the coast came to the bridge during the festival.
Her oldest friend from the theatre is coming to visit this year.
All the staff at the plant come to a picnic during the holiday.
That young engineer from the energy firm has come to lunch at last.
The school choir is drawing a large crowd from most nearby towns.

notes: Same verbs as the near misses: literal arrival stays near 0, which is the distinction. The pole fires on the verb itself, before 'to a halt' is seen, so the subject must set it up. Output promotes ' end', ' stop'.
